datasets.grain: one reported financial-statement line item in one immutable disclosure revision and statement scope

pit_contract.decision_time_rule: A fact is usable only when available_at <= decision_time. Preserve the source timestamp; when the official source exposes only a date or an untrusted timestamp, set available_at conservatively to the next exchange session open and record the fallback reason.
pit_contract.revision_rule: Never overwrite a filed value. A correction, supplementary filing, accounting error correction, or restatement creates a new document_revision_id and revision_id linked by supersedes_revision_id; earlier snapshots remain reproducible.

quality_gates: Every fact resolves to one hashed official document revision and one permanent security identity.
Primary keys are unique; consolidated and parent statements, report types, comparative roles and taxonomy versions never silently merge.
published_at and available_at are non-null; date-only disclosures use the documented conservative next-session fallback.
Balance-sheet accounting identity, statement totals/subtotals, cash-flow reconciliation and cross-statement sign/unit checks pass within declared tolerances.
Expected statements for each report type are either present or explicitly MISSING; missing facts remain null with reason codes.
Corrections and restatements form an acyclic revision chain and never mutate an older snapshot.
known_blockers: CNInfo and exchange web access does not by itself establish permission for automated bulk collection, local storage, or redistribution; endpoint-level terms must be recorded before ingestion.
Complete historical XBRL coverage and precise intraday publication timestamps are not guaranteed, especially for older filings.
General, bank, insurance and securities-company statement taxonomies require separate versioned mappings; PDF-only rows cannot be dropped when no canonical item exists.

datasets.grain: one reported or deterministically derived financial metric for one issuer, reporting period, scope, basis and revision

pit_contract.decision_time_rule: A metric is usable only when all inputs have available_at <= decision_time; derived available_at equals the maximum availability of its inputs and computation publication time.
pit_contract.revision_rule: Reported metrics inherit the filing revision. Any changed input, formula, comparison basis, or restatement creates a new revision_id and formula_version; previously published metric facts remain immutable.

quality_gates: Every derived metric resolves to immutable CORE-13 input facts, formula_version and input snapshot hashes.
available_at equals or exceeds the latest required input; no later filing or restatement is backdated.
Single-quarter values use comparable cumulative periods and Q4 equals annual minus Q3 YTD only when scope, taxonomy and revision basis match.
TTM, YoY and QoQ windows require complete comparable inputs; no interpolation, zero fill or silent denominator substitution is allowed.
Reported and derived versions are retained separately and material differences are CONFLICT, not overwritten.
General-company formulas are not applied to banks, insurers or securities firms without a versioned sector formula family.
known_blockers: CORE-13 has not yet produced an admitted immutable input snapshot.
Historical taxonomy changes and irregular reporting periods limit some single-quarter and growth reconstructions.
Cross-sector indicator names can share labels while having different definitions; sector-specific formula dictionaries remain to be implemented.

pit_contract.decision_time_rule: Use only an event revision whose available_at <= decision_time. Guidance ranges remain ranges; later express reports, periodic reports and corrections do not rewrite what was known earlier.
pit_contract.revision_rule: Each correction or updated estimate is a new event revision linked to the prior event through supersedes_revision_id. Actual periodic-report outcomes are calibration facts, not revisions of the historical guidance.

quality_gates: Every event and metric resolves to an official announcement payload and permanent security identity.
Guidance ranges preserve lower and upper bounds; midpoint is never a canonical L1 fact.
Correction chains are complete and acyclic; original guidance remains available for historical PIT reconstruction.
Metric signs, units, currencies, report periods and comparison periods are explicit and internally consistent.
Later periodic-report actuals may calculate forecast error but never overwrite the earlier guidance/express event.
Date-only or ambiguous publication times use the documented next-session fallback.
known_blockers: Historical announcement categories and templates differ across exchanges and years.
Narrative-only causes and uncertainty disclosures require versioned extraction with retained raw text.
Official bulk-access and storage permissions remain endpoint-specific and must be cleared before backfill.

pit_contract.decision_time_rule: Audit facts become usable only at the official report available_at. An opinion or matter disclosed later cannot be attached retrospectively to the report period for earlier decisions.
pit_contract.revision_rule: Corrected audit reports, reissued financial statements, accounting error corrections and changed internal-control conclusions create new revisions linked to the prior report; opinion taxonomies are versioned.

Emphasis, other matter, key audit matters and going-concern sections remain separate from the opinion code.
Financial-statement and internal-control audit opinions are never merged.
Every opinion and matter resolves to a signed official report hash, firm, report date, issuer and period.
Corrections/reissues form immutable revision chains; date-only publication times use a conservative availability fallback.
Unknown or unparsed opinion text is REVIEW, never defaulted to unmodified.
known_blockers: Older scanned PDFs can prevent reliable matter-level extraction and signer/report-number capture.
Audit terminology and report structure changed across standard revisions and internal-control regimes.
Official announcement bulk-access and storage terms must be cleared before historical backfill.

pit_contract.revision_rule: Each board proposal, shareholder approval, implementation announcement, cancellation or correction appends a stage revision linked by scheme_id and supersedes_revision_id. Implemented terms never overwrite proposal terms.

Terms are security-class aware and retain distribution base, exclusions, currency, tax wording and raw ratios.
Record, ex, payment and listing dates satisfy exchange-specific ordering rules or are explicitly missing/reviewed.
Per-share terms times the disclosed base reconcile to announced totals within rounding tolerance.
Implemented events reconcile bidirectionally with CORE-04 adjustment factors and CORE-07 share-capital changes without overwriting conflicts.
Corrections append a revision and never mutate the originally visible proposal or implementation.

Differential distributions, repurchased-share exclusions, multiple share classes and investor-specific tax rules require full-text evidence.
Official event-table and announcement bulk-use permissions remain to be documented before backfill.

quality_gates: Verbatim segment labels, source table positions, dimensions, report scope and units are retained even when normalization fails.
Revenue/cost/gross-profit arithmetic and disclosed totals reconcile within tolerance; unexplained residuals remain explicit.
Industry, product, geography, sales-mode and operating-segment dimensions are never summed across dimensions.
Mappings are issuer-specific, effective-dated and versioned; low-confidence mappings remain null/REVIEW rather than forced.
Restated tables and changed segment definitions append revisions and do not rewrite earlier PIT snapshots.
Segment facts resolve to admitted CORE-13 report revisions and official document hashes.

pit_contract.revision_rule: Official corrections or changed downloaded payloads append a revision. Derived cash returns pin the source series revision, compounding/day-count convention and formula version; no provider observation is overwritten.

quality_gates: Series identity pins provider, family, tenor, rate type, currency, methodology, day count and compounding convention.
Shibor includes O/N, 1W, 2W, 1M, 3M, 6M, 9M and 1Y; FR/FDR include 001/007/014; short government curves include at least 3M, 6M and 1Y when licensed and available.
Publication schedules are enforced as PIT cutoffs; observation_date is never substituted for published_at.
Expected business-day observations are present or explicitly MISSING/STALE; values and basis-point changes receive range/unit checks without assuming rates cannot be negative.
Official observations and cash-return projections are separate tables; research configuration must pin one series and formula version.
License gates are hard blockers: no raw, curated or derived publication is created from an unlicensed source.
known_blockers: CFETS states that copying, transmission, storage, use and derivative creation of its market data require written permission; public page visibility is insufficient.
ChinaBond pages reserve rights and direct users to data-product channels; automated retrieval and internal storage permission must be documented.
Historical endpoints, revision behavior and intraday publication timestamps require small-sample verification after permission is resolved.
PBOC 7-day reverse-repo rate is a policy-rate series, not interchangeable with a market risk-free return; research must explicitly choose its cash benchmark.

pit_contract.decision_time_rule: An exposure is usable only when every pinned input snapshot and the completed calculation have available_at <= decision_time. End-of-day exposures are intended for decisions no earlier than the next eligible session unless a stricter model contract says otherwise.
pit_contract.revision_rule: Input snapshot, universe, benchmark, methodology, window or code changes create a new model_version/formula_version and revision_id. Published exposures never overwrite older model snapshots.

fields.name: revision_id

quality_gates: All upstream snapshots pass their research-use, PIT, license and quality gates and are pinned by immutable hashes.
No input date or effective classification exceeds exposure_date; available_at is at least the latest upstream availability and calculation completion.
Descriptor formulas, benchmark/return variants, windows, lags, minimum observations, IPO/suspension treatment and market-cap basis are versioned.
Industry memberships use effective-dated CORE-11 classifications; index-based benchmarks use exact CORE-09/10 identities and return variants.
Nulls from insufficient history, suspension or missing inputs remain null with reason codes; no zero fill or hidden imputation is allowed.
L1 publishes raw descriptors only. Winsorisation, standardisation, industry neutralisation and missing-value imputation are separate L2 artifacts.
A deterministic rerun from the same input hashes and code version reproduces values within declared numerical tolerance.
known_blockers: Required admitted upstream snapshots for adjusted returns, tradability, share capital, index returns, industry classifications and risk-free rates do not yet exist.
